The source explicitly advises extending beyond product pages to page types including listicles, advertorials, and quiz funnels, in an effort to increase conversion rates on cold audiences.
The source supports a mobile-first CRO allocation and states that 10% of effort goes to desktop.

The candidate incorrectly makes the brand-specific 60–95% mobile-traffic observation a trigger or prerequisite. The source says “always mobile first”; the percentage is explanatory and explicitly varies by brand.
The source conditionally supports progressive split testing for 8- to 9-figure brands that have sufficient traffic and volume and set the program up correctly.

The asserted conflict with the revenue-per-visitor/contribution-per-visitor recommendation is not supported. The source itself presents both points: it discusses split tests that increase conversion rate while separately advising against using conversion rate as the primary business metric.
The source explicitly recommends installing Microsoft Clarity and says it provides heat maps and screen recordings of website visitors.
The recommendation is stated for “anyone,” so the candidate’s inclusive trigger does not impose a limiting prerequisite.
The source supports listing candidate changes, scoring impact, confidence, and ease out of 10, multiplying scores, sorting, and implementing the highest-scoring change first.
The candidate adds an unsupported lower bound of “1–10.” The source says each dimension is ranked “out of 10,” but does not state that 1 is the minimum possible score.

The warning accurately preserves the source’s condition—unethical overoptimization using dark-pattern persuasion—and its stated consequences: short-term lift followed by higher returns and chargebacks, lower repeat rates, and weaker LTV.
The warning itself is directly supported by the source’s skin-firmness example and the stated risks of returns, chargebacks, and lack of repeat purchase.

Its dependency on the dark-pattern warning is unsupported and misleading. The source advises against making undeliverable claims in general; it does not make that advice contingent on first engaging in unethical dark-pattern conversion tactics.
The source supports paying attention to returns, whether the product fulfills the need promoted by a new angle, 365-day LTV, and actual efficacy across messaging and angles.

The dependency on the dark-pattern warning is unsupported. The source presents this as a concern when testing or scaling new angles and concepts, not as a step contingent on unethical conversion-rate optimization.
The source also states that LTV can differ by the angle being pushed and by how well the product works under that angle; that operational qualification should be retained.
The claim and action are supported: the source says to look at revenue per visitor or contribution per visitor instead of treating conversion rate as the key metric.

The declared conflict with progressive split testing is not supported. The excerpt presents both recommendations and does not say that running conversion-focused split tests precludes measuring revenue per visitor or contribution per visitor.
The action accurately reproduces the source’s checklist for copy: remove doubt, be benefit-led, use a one-of-one angle, and handle objections using real customer language.
The source explicitly says to focus on positioning rather than discounting in order to keep margin, alongside having an offer worth converting on.
The source supports using real reviews, prioritizing photos, and not worrying about trust badges or other items that will not move the needle.
The candidate’s action omits the source’s distinct primary requirement that proof be specific and match the claim, despite including it in the claim and title.
The source supports the action to remove checkout friction.

“Maximize people actually getting through and purchasing” is stated by the source as the intended purpose of avoiding abandonment causes, not as a defined or verifiable completion criterion. Moreover, the referenced cart-abandonment reasons are absent from this excerpt.
